newsitem.title: USA: Chile is "litmus test" for US trade--Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: Chile is "litmus test" for US trade--Barshefsky.

text.p: Chile joining the North American Free Trade Agreement is seen as a "litmus test" for U.S. trade expansion in that region, U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday.

"Our ability to deliver on the commitment to Chile is seen, with some justification, as a litmus test for trade expansion and U.S. interest in this hemisphere," Barshefsky said in testimony prepared for a Senate Finance Committee hearing on her nomination.
U.S. exports to Latin America are estimated to exceed U.S. exports to Europe and Japan combined by 2010, she said.

The ability of the United States to negotiate comprehensive market opening agreements depends on the ability of the president and Congress to agree on the appropriate terms of "fast track" negotiating authority, Barshefsky said.
"The president believes that new negotiating authority is a key tool for advancing our nation's economic interests," Barshefsky said.
Barshefsky's nomination to the post has been complicated by a law barring anyone from the post if they have represented a foreign government on trade matters.
She represented Canadian lumber interests while she was a Washington lawyer.
Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said he supports a waiver of the law to allow Barshefsky to be confirmed.
She has been serving as acting U.S. Trade Representative since April last year.
